definition: Absent-mindedness is a state in which attention is so strongly focused on one thought or part of experience that other things in awareness are overlooked. In a more persistent or abnormal form, it involves habitual preoccupation, reduced awareness of surroundings, and difficulty shifting attention from one focus to another.
